html:
The Baraba Baraba are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Murray River country in northern Victoria and southern New South Wales, around Kerang and the lower Loddon and Wakool rivers. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land is river flats, swamps and lakes, rich in fish, waterbirds and plant foods. Little is recorded of them in detail. Neighbours on the map include the Yorta Yorta, the Wemba Wemba and the Wadi Wadi. Squatters took up the Murray frontage from the 1840s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
